hero.title: What runs where
hero.lede: Windows is supported today. macOS, Linux and headless rendering are in preview: the work is in PowerBGInfo pull request #91 and ships with the next release, together with new DesktopManager and ChartForgeX releases.
hero.check: A rendered image does not prove that a desktop accepted it. `Get-BGInfoCapability` and the CLI's `--doctor` report what the current desktop can do before you apply anything.

howto.title: Run it on your platform
howto.body: PowerBGInfo performs one run and exits. Each platform needs the same three decisions: where it runs, which session it runs in, and what refreshes it.

guides.lede: The supported platform today. Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7, the desktop and the lock screen, every monitor and, with elevation, every profile on the machine.
steps: Install the module from the PowerShell Gallery for yourself, or for all users on machines that run it unattended.
Build a layout in PowerShell or JSON and render it with `-Target File` until it looks right.
Choose `Wallpaper`, `LogonScreen` or `Both` with `-Target`. `-AllUsers` also writes the wallpaper into every local profile.
Refresh it at sign-in with Task Scheduler, Group Policy, Intune or Configuration Manager.

guides.lede: Preview. GNOME through GSettings and KDE Plasma through its D-Bus scripting interface. On any other desktop PowerBGInfo renders a file and leaves applying it to you.
steps: Install PowerShell 7.4 or later and the module.
Open a terminal inside the graphical session of the user who will see the wallpaper. An SSH session, root or a system account cannot change that desktop.
Run `Get-BGInfoCapability` to see which desktop backend it found.
Set the image size with `New-BGInfoBackground -Width` and `-Height`. The GNOME and KDE adapters do not report physical screen sizes.
GNOME uses one image for every screen, so keep monitor index 0. KDE also needs index 0 when it cannot list its screens.
To refresh it, run the command from a systemd user timer or an XDG autostart entry.

guides.lede: Preview. `-Target File` never reads or changes a wallpaper, so it runs on a server, in a container or in a CI job with no desktop at all.
steps: Use `-Target File` with `New-BGInfo`, `-NoApply` with `Invoke-BGInfo` or `--no-apply` with the CLI.
Give the size with `New-BGInfoBackground -Width` and `-Height`. There is no monitor to measure.
Install the fonts the layout uses on the build host. Fonts resolve where the image renders.
Keep paths in JSON relative, so the same file works on Windows, macOS and Linux.

limits.title: Limits to plan around
limits.body: These hold for the preview in pull request #91. Each one fails or warns plainly instead of guessing.

items.title: Lock screen and all users are Windows only
items.body: On macOS and Linux a lock-screen or all-users request fails before anything renders or changes. Use `Wallpaper` for the current desktop or `File` for an image.

items.title: HEIC wallpapers become a plain backdrop
items.body: When the current macOS wallpaper is HEIC or another format the renderer cannot read, PowerBGInfo warns and draws on a plain background. Name a PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, PPM or TIFF image, or use a generated background, to keep a photo.

items.title: Fonts come from the rendering host
items.body: Text uses the fonts installed where the image renders. Install the same licensed fonts on every host where the type must match.

items.title: Windows paths do not travel
items.body: A Windows-rooted path such as `C:\Wallpapers\base.jpg` in JSON is rejected on macOS and Linux. Use relative paths, with either slash, or a local absolute path.

items.title: It must run in the user's session
items.body: Changing a wallpaper needs the graphical session of the user who will see it. An SSH session, a system account or an administrator token does not replace it.

items.title: Policy can still refuse
items.body: A managed-device policy can block a change that the backend reports as supported. Check the result, not only the render.

study.label: Under study
study.title: iPhone and iPad
study.lede: We are looking at whether PowerBGInfo is useful for Apple mobile devices. Nothing here ships, and nothing here is promised.

points.title: What stops it
points.body: iOS and iPadOS give apps no way to set the wallpaper, so PowerBGInfo cannot run on the device and change it.

points.title: What could work
points.body: Device management can set a wallpaper on supervised devices. Microsoft Intune and Jamf are two services that offer it. What each service supports differs, so check yours.

points.title: The idea
points.body: PowerBGInfo renders one image per device from your inventory, with the asset tag, the owner and a helpdesk QR code, and your MDM delivers it.

questions: How each MDM takes an image per device rather than one image for a group.
Which screen sizes to render for the models in a fleet.
How often the image needs refreshing when an owner changes.
